paper.title: Context-Aware Proactive Content Caching With Service Differentiation in Wireless Networks

settings.name_in_paper: Context-aware proactive caching (contextual multi-armed bandit, select m of |F| files)
unmapped: Demands take values in [0, R_max] (not [0,1]); bounded after rescaling
Multiple contexts (up to U_max users) arrive per round, each in [0,1]^D; context sequence arbitrary
Expected demand mu_f(x) is Holder continuous in context with constants L, alpha
Known service weights v_s and file weights w_f (weighted rewards)
Learner must know Holder exponent alpha and context dimension D to tune K(t), h_T
settings.definition_quote: The number of times a user with context vector $x\in \mathcal{X}$ requests a file $f\in F$ within one time slot is a random variable with unknown distribution... The random demand is assumed to take values in $[0,R_{\max}]$... R(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T \sum _{j=1}^m \sum _{i=1}^{U_t} v_{s_{t,i}} ( w_{f_j^\ast} E(d_{f_j^\ast}(x_{t,i})) - E(w_{c_{t,j}}d_{c_{t,j}}(x_{t,i},t)))

settings.name_in_paper: Rating-based context-aware proactive caching with missing ratings
unmapped: Reward is rating times demand, in [0, r_max*R_max]
Each user's rating revealed only with probability q (missing feedback)
Multiple Holder-continuous contexts per round in [0,1]^D
settings.definition_quote: Let $q\in (0,1)$ be the probability that a user reveals his rating after requesting a file.

algorithms.name: m-CAC (Context-Aware Proactive Caching with Cache Size m)

bound.expression_latex: O\left(v_{\max} w_{\max} m U_{\max}R_{\max} |F| T^{\frac{2\alpha + D}{3\alpha + D}} \log(T) \right)

symbols.U_max: maximum number of simultaneously connected users
symbols.R_max: maximum demand per user per slot

conditions: Assumption 1: mu_f is Holder continuous with constants L>0, alpha>0
demands independent across users and files and of past

source.label: Theorem_Regret
source.quote: Let $K(t) = t^{\frac{2\alpha}{3 \alpha + D}} \log (t)$ and $h_T = \ceil{T^{\frac{1}{3\alpha + D}}}$. If m-CAC is run with these parameters and Assumption \ref{Ass_Hoelder} holds true, the leading order of the regret $R(T)$ is $O\left(v_{\max} w_{\max} m U_{\max}R_{\max} |F| T^{\frac{2\alpha + D}{3\alpha + D}} \log(T) \right)$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected demands against per-round oracle top-m files. 'Leading order' bound. Also stated for ratings always available with extra r_max factor (in text, not a theorem).

bound.expression_latex: O\left(\frac{1}{q} v_{\max} w_{\max} r_{\max} m U_{\max}R_{\max} |F| T^{\frac{2\alpha + D}{3\alpha + D}} \log(T) \right)

symbols.q: probability a user reveals a rating
symbols.U_max: maximum number of simultaneously connected users
symbols.R_max: maximum demand per user per slot

conditions: Assumption 1 holds for tilde d_f(x) = r_f(x) d_f(x)
rating revealed with probability q in (0,1)

source.label: Theorem_Regret_Rating
source.quote: Let $K(t) = t^{\frac{2\alpha}{3 \alpha + D}} \log (t)$ and $h_T = \ceil{T^{\frac{1}{3\alpha + D}}}$. If m-CAC is run with these parameters with respect to $\tilde{d}_f(x)$, Assumption \ref{Ass_Hoelder} holds true for $\tilde{d}_f(x)$ and a user reveals his rating with probability $q$, the leading order of the regret $R(T)$ is $O\left(\frac{1}{q} v_{\max} w_{\max} r_{\max} m U_{\max}R_{\max} |F| T^{\frac{2\alpha + D}{3\alpha + D}} \log(T) \right)$.
